summary: Game crashes when replacing a block with a wall with blockstate up:false
description: Give yourself a wall using give @p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1 Then, place a block with no other blocks around it, and press left and right click at the same time while looking at that block and holding the wall. Then, crash.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Give yourself a wall with the command: `/give @p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1`.
3. Place a block with no other blocks around it.
4. While looking at the placed block, press and hold both the left and right mouse buttons simultaneously while holding the wall.
5. Observe that the game crashes.
Observed Behavior: The game experiences a crash when attempting to replace a block with a wall that has the blockstate up set to false. To reproduce this issue, a player can use the command to give themselves a brick wall with the specific blockstate tag, which is achieved by entering give @p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1. After obtaining the wall, the player should place a block in an empty area where no other blocks are nearby. The crash occurs when the player simultaneously presses the left and right mouse buttons while looking at the placed block and holding the wall item. This action leads to an unexpected termination of the game, indicating a critical bug that requires attention. It is important to note that the issue is not limited to brick walls, as it has been confirmed to occur with any type of wall.
Expected Behavior: When following the reproduction steps, the game should not crash when attempting to replace a block with a wall that has the blockstate up set to "false." Instead, the wall should be placed successfully without any errors, allowing the player to interact with the block as intended. This behavior should remain consistent across all relevant game versions, ensuring a stable gameplay experience.
